genZNote: Bilateral parotid swelling is basically the diagnosis handing itself to you.

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human salivary gland and respiratory epithelium

identificationClues: Bilateral (or unilateral) parotid gland swelling is the classic clinical clue
PCR of a buccal/oral swab or saliva is the preferred confirmatory test
MMR vaccination has substantially reduced incidence, though outbreaks still occur in close-contact settings (e.g. college campuses)

diseases: Orchitis (testicular inflammation, a recognized complication, especially post-pubertal males)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Respiratory droplets and direct contact with saliva
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Vaccine-preventable (MMR); outbreaks continue to occur periodically in close-contact settings, sometimes including previously vaccinated individuals as vaccine-induced immunity can wane
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: PCR of a buccal/oral swab collected early in illness is more sensitive than serology alone, particularly in previously vaccinated individuals with a modified clinical course

examFacts.importantTest: PCR of buccal/oral swab or saliva
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Classic bilateral parotid gland swelling distinguishes it clinically from most other viral respiratory infections
